title: TuHURA Biosciences Provides First Look at Data from its Open-Label Study of IFx-2.0 as an Adjunctive Therapy to Keytruda® in First Line Treatment of Patients with Deep Seated Metastatic Merkel Cell Carcinoma
summary: Preliminary results demonstrate major objective tumor responses in first 3 patients at 6 months  Company to…...
body_markdown:
*Preliminary results demonstrate major objective tumor responses in first 3 patients at 6 months*


*Company to host a webcast today, October 26, 2026, at 8:30 am ET*


TAMPA, Fla.


, Oct. 26, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- TuHURA Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ: HURA) ("TuHURA" or the "Company"), a Phase 3 immuno-oncology company developing novel therapeutics to overcome resistance to cancer immunotherapy, today announced initial data from the first three patients in its open-label study of IFx-2.0 as an adjunctive therapy to Keytruda® in first-line treatment of metastatic Merkel Cell Carcinoma (MCC). Results showed that each patient achieved a major objective anti-tumor response, with all three responses meeting the criteria for partial response (PR) under RECIST v.1.1 criteria. All responses were durable, as each of the responses were ongoing at the protocol-specified six-month assessment.


The Phase 1b/2a trial of IFx-2.0 is a multicenter, open-label trial designed to assess the safety and feasibility of IFx-2.0 as adjunctive therapy to Keytruda® (pembrolizumab) when administered into deep seated and/or bulky tumors accessible with CT or ultrasound guided administration in the front-line treatment of adult patients with metastatic MCC. The trial is designed to initially enroll a total of nine patients with visceral tumors including hepatic, pulmonary, or retroperitoneal or other deep seated locations using CT or ultrasound guided administration where standard-size injection needles are unable to effectively administer the intended dose of IFx-2.0.


Each patient received IFx-2.0 (0.1 mg) injected into a single deep-seated or bulky tumor once a week for three weeks. Within 48 hours of the first IFx-2.0 injection, patients received Keytruda®, followed by Keytruda® every three weeks until the earlier of disease progression, toxicity, or 2 years. Keytruda® is approved as the front-line standard of care for patients with advanced or metastatic MCC.


The primary endpoint of the study is safety and feasibility of IFx-2.0 therapy evaluated 28 days following the last dose of IFx-2.0, which is 49 days from the first IFx-2.0 infusion. The study will also evaluate key secondary endpoints, including efficacy per RECIST1.1 criteria at three and six months.


"While preliminary and only reported in 3 patients, these results highlight that it is feasible to utilize CT or ultrasound guided administration of IFx-2.0 safely to patients with large bulky and or deep-seated tumors. This is also the first time we have administered IFx-2.0 with Keytruda® in the front line treatment setting of patients with metastatic MCC and may serve as a proxy to the potential response rates in the ongoing randomized placebo controlled Phase 3 trial, which is also being conducted in the front line treatment of patients with advanced or metastatic MCC as an adjunct with Keytruda®," said Dr. James Bianco, President and Chief Executive Officer at TuHURA Biosciences. "Approximately 30% of patients with metastatic MCC present without cutaneous or superficial nodal involvement. If we continue to see this high response rate in patients in this trial, we will explore the potential to expand the number of patients in the trial and discuss with the FDA its potential to supplement the ongoing Phase 3 trial, should that study successfully meet the primary endpoint. We look forward to additional patient data in the coming months, and we will seek to present the data at an appropriate scientific conference next year."

**About TuHURA Biosciences, Inc.**


TuHURA Biosciences, Inc. (NASDAQ: HURA) is a Phase 3 immuno-oncology company developing novel technologies to overcome primary and acquired resistance to cancer immunotherapy, two of the most common reasons cancer immunotherapies fail to work or stop working in the majority of patients with cancer.


TuHURA's lead innate immune agonist, IFx-2.0, is designed to overcome primary resistance to checkpoint inhibitors. TuHURA has initiated a single randomized placebo-controlled Phase 3 registration trial of IFx-2.0 administered as an adjunctive therapy to Keytruda® (pembrolizumab) compared to Keytruda® plus placebo in first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic Merkel Cell Carcinoma.


In addition to its innate immune agonist product candidates, TuHURA is developing TBS-2025, its VISTA-inhibiting mAb in a Phase 1b clinical trial in patients with *mut* NPM1 r/r AML, a molecularly defined subgroup that represents approximately 35% of patients with AML. TuHURA is also leveraging its Delta Opioid Receptor technology to develop first-in-class, bi-specific, bi-functional antibody drug conjugates (ADCs) targeting Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cells to inhibit their immune-suppressing effects on the tumor microenvironment to prevent T cell exhaustion and acquired resistance to checkpoint inhibitors and cellular therapies.
